Dolphins are regarded as the friendliest creatures in the sea and stories of them helping drowning sailors have been common since Roman times. The more we learn about dolphins, the more we realize that their society is more complex than people previously imagined. They look after other dolphins when they are ill, care for pregnant mothers and protect the weakest in the community, as we do. Some scientists have suggested that dolphins have a language but it is much more probable that they communicate with each other without needing words. Could any of these mammals be more intelligent than man? Certainly the most common argument in favour of man's superiority over them that we can kill them more easily than they can kill us is the least satisfactory. On the contrary, the more we discover about these remarkable creatures, the less we appear superior when we destroy them.


The fact that the writer of the passage thinks that we can kill dolphins more easily than they can kill us.

  1. means that they are better adapted to their environment than we are
  2. shows that dolphins have a very sophisticated form of communication
  3. proves that dolphins are not the most intelligent species at sea
  4. does not mean that we are superior to them

Let $\text{A, B}$ be two finite, non-empty sets, with cardinality of $\text{A, B}$ as $m, n$ respectively.

Let $\mathrm{f}: \mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{B}$ be a function with domain $\mathrm{A}$ and co-domain $\mathrm{B}$. Let $r$ be the cardinality of range of $f.$

We define a relation $\mathrm{R}$ on $\mathrm{A}$, defined by $(x, y) \in \mathrm{R} \Leftrightarrow \mathrm{f}(x)=\mathrm{f}(y)$.

Which of the following statements is true?

  1. $\mathrm{R}$ is not an equivalence relation.
  2. $\mathrm{R}$ is an equivalence relation having $r$ equivalence classes.
  3. $\mathrm{R}$ is an equivalence relation having $m$ equivalence classes.
  4. $\mathrm{R}$ is an equivalence relation having $n$ equivalence classes.

If we have $m$ vectors $u_1, u_2, \ldots, u_m$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, then we can form the matrix $\text{A}$ whose columns are $u_1, \ldots, u_m$. Let $\text{B}$ be the echelon form of $\text{A}$.

Suppose we are given the following matrix $\text{B}$ :
$$
\left(\begin{array}{cccc}
3 & 0 & -1 & 5 \\
0 & 0 & 2 & -1 \\
0 & 0 & 0 & 0
\end{array}\right)
$$
Since $\text{B}$ is the echelon form of $\text{A}$, both $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ have the same size $-3$ rows and $4$ columns.


Which if the following is/are CORRECT?

  3. $\text{A} x=0$ and $\text{B} x=0$ have the same solutions.
  4. If we erase the last row of zeros in $\text{B}$ then the columns of the resulting matrix would be linearly independent.

Consider the following function which takes node of a binary tree as an argument and tries to find something.

int findsomething(Node p) {
    if (p == NULL) return -1;
    if (p→left == NULL)
        return 1 + findsomething(p→right);
    if (p→right == NULL)
        return 1 + findsomething(p→left);
    else
        return 1 + min(findsomething(p→left), findsomething(p→right));
}

What does the above function try to calculate?

  1. Level of nearest leaf to root
  2. Level of farthest leaf to root
  3. Total number of nodes in left subtree of root
  4. Total number of nodes in one of subtree of root whichever is having lesser nodes.
